correctness.rationale: The normalized monomial eigenvalue formula is direct beta-prime integration. Exact even/odd digit decompositions give sums of probability Cantor-stage measures. Local growth #Cantor integers <= C(1+T)^delta with delta<1 gives uniform tails. Gamma-ratio and exp(-k/(1+t)) bounds yield degree-uniform renormalized eigenvalue decay \(C_b(k+1)^{\delta-1}\). This justifies passing fixed-degree limits through the spectral supremum. All b>0 and boundaries n>=0 are explicit; finite checker is corroboration only.

value.rationale: The motivating 2022 radial Bergman fractal uncertainty theorem determined only a decay exponent up to multiplicative constants. Determining actual leading norm coefficients, including the parity-dependent limit representations and control of high monomial degrees, removes the main quantitative ambiguity in that natural problem. A localized finite eigenvalue calculation alone would not do so; the spectral-tail compactness and explicit Cantor-integer measure are essential structural contributions. The constants are approximable with provable digit and degree truncation errors.
